Aggregate a coupling or co-citation network at the level of entities

Source: R/entity_network.R
entity_network.Rd

Builds the edges of a coupling (or co-citation) network whose nodes are not documents but entities that aggregate documents: authors, journals, institutions, countries... It is not a new measure of proximity: it takes the measures of biblio_coupling() (or of biblio_cocitation()) and computes them for entities instead of documents. Since an entity publishes several documents, it can cite the same reference several times, and the function takes this into account: citing a reference ten times is more significant than citing it once. The counts are combined with the minimum rule of Zhao and Strotmann (2008) .

Usage

entity_network(
  dt,
  source,
  ref,
  entity,
  network = c("coupling", "cocitation"),
  method = c("angle", "strength", "similarity", "jaccard", "vladutz"),
  weight_threshold = 1,
  output_in_character = FALSE
)

Arguments

dt

A data frame or a data.table of direct citations, one row per link between a citing document and a cited reference. It is not modified.

source

Character scalar. The column of the citing documents. Needed to count the documents, not to define the nodes (except for network = "cocitation", see the details).

ref

Character scalar. The column of the cited references.

entity

Character scalar. The column of the entities that are the nodes of the network (authors, journals, institutions...). With network = "coupling" it describes the citing documents (source); with network = "cocitation" it describes the cited references (ref). A document can appear with several entities (one row per entity and reference).

network

"coupling" (default): the entities are linked when their documents cite the same references. "cocitation": they are linked when their references are cited by the same documents.

method

The weighting method, one of "angle" (default), "strength", "similarity", "jaccard" and "vladutz": see the details, and biblio_coupling() for their document-level versions.

weight_threshold

Number. The minimum number of shared references for two entities to be linked (1 by default). With large entities such as journals, a higher value is advisable.

output_in_character

Logical. If TRUE, from and to are character columns (FALSE by default for this function: they keep the type of the entity column).

Value

A data.table with one row per pair of entities: from, to, the weight, the original identifiers in Source and Target, and the Weighting_method (the method). Each pair appears once, with Source < Target.

Details

Write \(C_{Aj}\) for the number of times entity \(A\) cites reference \(j\) (the number of its documents citing \(j\)), \(N\) for the number of citing documents in the table, \(f_j\) for the number of documents citing \(j\), and \(L(A) = \sum_j C_{Aj}\) for the total number of citations made by \(A\). Write also \(m_{AB}(g) = \sum_{j} \min(C_{Aj}, C_{Bj}) \, g_j\), the overlap of the two entities, with the references weighted by \(g_j\). According to method, the weight of the tie between \(A\) and \(B\) is

  • "angle", with \(g_j = 1\): $$w_{AB} = \frac{m_{AB}(1)}{\sqrt{L(A) \, L(B)}}$$

  • "strength", with \(g_j = \log(N / f_j)\): $$w_{AB} = \frac{m_{AB}(g)}{L(A) \, L(B)}$$

  • "similarity", with \(g_j = \log(N / f_j)\) and \(S(A) = \sum_j C_{Aj} \log(N / f_j)\): $$w_{AB} = \frac{m_{AB}(g)}{\sqrt{S(A) \, S(B)}}$$

  • "jaccard", with \(g_j = 1\): $$w_{AB} = \frac{m_{AB}(1)}{L(A) + L(B) - m_{AB}(1)}$$ which is the ratio of the sum of the minima to the sum of the maxima of the counts (the weighted Jaccard index);

  • "vladutz", with \(g_j = 1 / f_j\): $$w_{AB} = \frac{4 \, m_{AB}(g)}{L(A) + L(B)}$$

The sums run over the references cited by both entities, and \(L\), \(S\) over all the references of the entity. The minimum of the two counts is the number of times the two entities cite the reference "together" (Zhao and Strotmann 2008) . The package follows the paper for the minimum rule with the coupling angle and strength; the other methods are the same extension, applied to the measures of coupling_similarity(), coupling_jaccard() and coupling_vladutz() (the similarity is still bounded by 1, since \(\min(C_{Aj}, C_{Bj}) \leq \sqrt{C_{Aj} C_{Bj}}\) and by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality). With a single citation per entity and reference, each method gives back the document-level measure. \(f_j\) counts citing documents, not entities, so that a document with several authors is not counted several times. References cited by a single entity cannot create a tie and are ignored in the overlaps, but they count in \(L\).

Co-citation. With network = "cocitation", the roles of source and ref are swapped, as in biblio_cocitation(): the nodes are the entities of the cited references, and the entity column must describe ref (the author or the journal of the cited reference). Two entities are co-cited when documents cite references of both. The formulas above apply with the roles exchanged: \(C_{Aj}\) is the number of references of \(A\) cited by document \(j\).

The weight_threshold applies to the number of references shared by two entities (each counted once, whatever the number of times it is cited). The table of the user is not modified, rows with a missing identifier are dropped with a warning, and a zero-row table is returned, with a warning, if no reference is shared (or if no pair reaches weight_threshold). The memory warning of coupling_strength() applies.

Why use it in research

Coupling at the level of authors (author bibliographic coupling, (Zhao and Strotmann 2008) ), journals or institutions maps who relies on the same literature, whatever the documents they publish. With network = "cocitation", it maps which authors, journals or institutions are cited together, as in author co-citation analysis. It is a way to study the structure of a discipline through its journals or its authors, with fewer and denser nodes than the document-level network. Because entities are aggregates of documents, check that they are not too heterogeneous (a generalist journal citing everything is coupled with everyone), and that the number of documents per entity is large enough to give a stable bibliography. An article with several authors appears once for each of its authors: the same document then contributes to several entities.

Intuition

Think of an entity (say a journal) as one big bibliography made of the bibliographies of all its documents, in which a reference appears as many times as the entity's documents cite it. Two journals are close when their big bibliographies overlap. Overlap is measured reference by reference by the smaller of the two counts: if journal A cites a reference 10 times and journal B twice, they share it twice (B is the limit). The methods then differ in what they do with these overlaps, as their document-level counterparts: "angle" only counts them and normalises by the sizes of the two big bibliographies; "strength" counts a shared rare reference more than a shared classic; "similarity" does the same but normalises by the "informational size" of each big bibliography, to give a cosine that cannot exceed 1; "jaccard" compares the overlap with the union of the two big bibliographies; "vladutz" discounts popular references steeply.

References

Zhao D, Strotmann A (2008). “Author Bibliographic Coupling: Another Approach to Citation-Based Author Knowledge Network Analysis.” Proceedings of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 45(1), 1–10. https://asistdl.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/meet.2008.1450450292.

Examples

library(biblionetwork)
Ref_stagflation$Citing_ItemID_Ref <- as.character(Ref_stagflation$Citing_ItemID_Ref)
# merging the references data with the citing author information in Nodes_stagflation
entity_citations <- merge(Ref_stagflation,
                          Nodes_stagflation,
                          by.x = "Citing_ItemID_Ref",
                          by.y = "ItemID_Ref")

entity_network(entity_citations,
                source = "Citing_ItemID_Ref",
                ref = "ItemID_Ref",
                entity = "Author.y",
                method = "angle")

                    entity = "Journal", network = "cocitation", weight_threshold = 2))
